title: Management styles
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-01T14:55:58Z write: failed the content check, writing again

match.reason: The bank point covers only three styles (autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire), while the new point requires the full five-step continuum that adds persuasive, consultative and participative, so it is broader and not the same card.

draft.title: Management styles
card: A management style is the way a manager makes decisions and deals with staff. The styles run along a line, and staff get more say at each step.
the manager decides alone and tells staff what to do. Persuasive is next: the manager still decides alone, but explains the reasons to win support.
the manager asks staff for views before deciding, but makes the final decision.
staff share in the decision, and the group decides together. Laissez-faire goes further: staff decide largely for themselves.
draft.remember: From autocratic to laissez-faire, staff have more say in decisions at each step.

a.q: A manager asks staff for ideas about a new roster, then chooses the roster alone. Which style is this?
a.why: The manager asks for views first, then makes the final call alone, which is consultative. Participative is tempting, but there staff share in making the decision.
a.clue: Who makes the final decision after the staff are asked?

b.q: Priya announces a new opening time, then spends ten minutes explaining why it helps customers. She did not ask staff beforehand. Which style is this?
b.why: Priya decided alone and then explained her reasons to win support, which is persuasive. Autocratic is tempting, but an autocratic manager just tells staff what to do without explaining reasons to win them over.
b.clue: Did Priya ask for views before or only explain after?
